purpose: Measure operator-bridge RAM, CPU, and local interaction latency reproducibly on the target Windows operator workstation without weakening the UX-08 no-content boundary.
design_acceptance: The benchmark contract and budgets are sufficient to proceed to UX-10. Empirical target-machine results remain mandatory before UX-13 production design freeze and before raising the default active-session cap.
security_invariants: No ChatGPT DOM, response text, accessibility tree, screenshots, raw URLs, cookies, tokens, or page-content telemetry may be collected.
No synthetic paste, typing, Enter, Send, or mouse automation is introduced for measurement.
Real-account calibration, when eventually run, remains manual at Ctrl+V + Enter and is gated by the UX-08/UX-12 OpenAI policy review.
Primary resource telemetry is OS process telemetry; browser-internal process managers are diagnostic only and are not persisted with page labels.

evidence_basis.relevance: Firefox can unload inactive tabs while retaining tabstrip/session state; active tabs cannot be discarded.
Firefox exposes rough per-process memory/CPU diagnostics through about:processes; primary cross-browser benchmark still uses OS metrics.
Windows process objects expose working-set and pageable/private memory metrics suitable for external collection.
Chrome may deactivate inactive tabs; live-tab comparison disables Memory Saver for parity and records its state.

evidence_basis.source: Microsoft WebView2 process model / performance guidance
evidence_basis.relevance: A custom Windows worker shell can embed the Edge/WebView2 runtime; it remains multi-process, and sharing one CoreWebView2Environment across tab-like views is the documented memory-efficient pattern.
Embedded user-agents can be disallowed for Google OAuth. Any custom worker browser that cannot complete the user's normal ChatGPT authentication flow without bypasses is non-viable.

target_environment.os: target Windows operator workstation; exact edition/build recorded per run
target_environment.power_mode: AC power; fixed Windows power mode recorded
target_environment.network: same network path for compared latency trials; browser-memory trials do not use response-content timing
target_environment.browser_versions: record exact Firefox, Chrome, and any selected custom-shell engine/runtime version
target_environment.display: record monitor count/scaling only as context; no screen capture
target_environment.reboot_policy: preferred fresh login or confirmed quiescent browser state before each complete replicate
target_environment.background_noise: record top-level system available memory and CPU load; reject sample windows with sustained unrelated CPU load above 20% of total CPU

process_measurement.isolation_rule: For each adapter trial, no unrelated processes using the same browser/runtime identity may run in the benchmark Windows user session unless the collector has a reviewed process-group attribution mechanism that requires no page inspection.

primary_memory_metric.definition: sum WorkingSet64 across all benchmark browser executable processes in the user session, converted to MiB

secondary_memory_metric.definition: sum PrivateMemorySize64 across all benchmark browser executable processes in the user session, converted to MiB
secondary_memory_metric.rationale: captures private committed memory and helps diagnose working-set trimming

helper_metrics: helper CPU delta normalized to one logical CPU
process_measurement.browser_cpu_metric: CPU-time delta over sample interval normalized as percent of one logical CPU

simulator_profile.role: deterministic primary regression workload once fake-ChatGPT simulator exists

real_chatgpt_calibration.role: target-machine calibration only after real-account policy/product gate
real_chatgpt_calibration.procedure: Human authenticates and establishes standardized bounded worker chats manually. Resource collector observes processes only; it does not inspect page content.

browser_comparison.firefox_profile: fresh/dedicated WorkspaceWorkers benchmark profile; only reviewed bridge extension enabled when testing extension overhead
browser_comparison.chrome_profile: fresh temporary benchmark profile; no unrelated extensions
browser_comparison.live_tab_parity: Chrome Memory Saver disabled for 0/1/2/4 live-tab comparison; its state is recorded
comparison_metrics: incremental working set above 0-worker-tab browser baseline
browser_comparison.review_trigger: Reopen the dedicated-Firefox ADR if Firefox fails its frozen budgets, materially trails Chrome, or a viable custom worker shell beats Firefox by at least 20% on two-worker p95 working set or by at least 25% on cold-start/reuse latency without weakening security, authentication, maintainability, or recovery.

custom_worker_browser_candidate.objective: Allow a purpose-built worker shell to compete with Firefox rather than assuming a general-purpose browser is permanently optimal.
custom_worker_browser_candidate.initial_windows_candidate: WebView2-based shell sharing one CoreWebView2Environment across worker views
secondary_candidates: other maintained browser engine with explicit Windows embedding support
required_properties: Preserve manual Ctrl+V + Enter and UX-08 no-content boundary.
Expose browser lifecycle/focus/navigation-origin metadata without DOM/output inspection.
Provide isolated persistent user-data/profile state for WorkspaceWorkers.
Support multiple logical worker views with deterministic slot/generation binding.
Support unload/suspend/close semantics sufficient for the two-live/default and four-live/burst policies.
Complete normal ChatGPT authentication manually without cookie copying, token extraction, private endpoint use, or safeguard bypass.
hard_rejection_conditions: Normal authentication is blocked by the embedded user-agent and would require cookie/session transfer or product-policy circumvention.
The shell requires ChatGPT DOM/content automation to recover or route sessions.
Security patch/update burden is materially worse than the Firefox-extension design without a compensating measured benefit.
custom_worker_browser_candidate.benchmark_rule: If UX-12 produces a viable custom shell, run the same 0/1/2/4-worker, cold-start, reuse, restore/suspend, and helper-overhead scenarios before UX-13.

scenarios: Firefox profile open with zero worker tabs
Firefox with 1 live worker tab
Firefox with 2 live worker tabs
Firefox with 4 live worker tabs
Chrome baseline profile with zero worker tabs
Chrome with 1 live worker tab
Chrome with 2 live worker tabs
Chrome with 4 live worker tabs
If UX-12 selects a viable custom worker shell: custom shell open with zero worker views
If selected: custom shell with 1 live worker view
If selected: custom shell with 2 live worker views
If selected: custom shell with 4 live worker views
scenario_groups.order_policy: Firefox and Chrome remain mandatory baselines. If a custom shell exists, rotate all three adapter orders across replicates; within each adapter run 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 4 live workers.

scenarios: native helper idle with browser closed
Firefox zero-worker-tab profile without bridge extension
Firefox zero-worker-tab profile with bridge extension connected
Firefox two-live-tab profile with helper + extension connected
Start with 4 live managed worker tabs; leave one active and discard the other 3 through reviewed Firefox tabs.discard mechanics; sample after settle.
Restore one discarded tab and resample.
Restore all discarded tabs and resample.
scenario_groups.note: The active tab is never passed to tabs.discard because Firefox does not discard the active tab.

scenario_groups.metric: hotkey edge -> LOCAL_PREPARED / exact target focused and clipboard write confirmed
scenario_groups.precondition: Firefox running; target trusted managed tab already live
Firefox running; target trusted managed tab discarded
Firefox running; new managed tab required

scenarios: hotkey edge -> helper callback entered
clipboard write call begin -> success result
browser activate command -> extension success receipt
no-work hotkey edge -> quiet no-action completion

active_session_policy.rationale: Preserves the UX-04 two-general-slot design, permits one SENT/UNCONFIRMED worker plus one independently serviceable worker, and bounds browser memory before empirical calibration.
burst_cap_conditions: Only workflow-required role isolation or explicit benchmark scenario may exceed the default of 2.
No default cap increase above 2 until real target-machine measurements pass the four-tab resource budget.
Idle trusted sessions above the default live cap should be candidates for DISCARD rather than retirement when continuity remains safe.
reopen_conditions: discarding 3 of 4 tabs reclaims less than 25% total working set
restore p95 exceeds 2500 ms enough to make discard ergonomically counterproductive

reject_if: authentication/recovery incident occurs during resource window
unrelated same-name browser process is present
sustained unrelated CPU exceeds environment threshold
collector cannot attribute helper/browser processes without page inspection
security boundary would need to be weakened to collect a metric
do_not_reject_for: normal small run-to-run browser process-count variation

result_record_shape.machine_fingerprint: non-secret hash of recorded hardware/OS descriptor
result_record_shape.browser_version: browser or embedded runtime version string|null

execution_state.blocker: The v0 helper/extension, deterministic fake-worker workload, and any custom-shell spike do not exist yet. Real ChatGPT calibration is also gated by UX-12 implementation and a fresh OpenAI policy/product review.
execution_state.next_measurement_owner: UX-10 simulator + UX-12 implementation spike, with final calibration before UX-13 design freeze
